requirement.title: Fix hook scripts — correct session/pane extraction
requirement.description: Replace broken $TMUX_PANE usage in hook scripts with tmux display-message to correctly extract session name and window.pane target. Both gmux-status.sh and gmux-notify.sh must be fixed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a hook script runs inside a tmux pane in session "arcforge" window 1 pane 1, when the script extracts session and pane values, then SESSION="arcforge" and PANE="1.1" (via tmux display-message -p).
Given tmux display-message fails (not inside tmux), when the script runs, then SESSION and PANE fall back to "unknown" and the script exits 0.
Given the socket at /tmp/gmux.sock does not exist, when the hook script runs, then it exits 0 without error output (unchanged from current behavior).

requirement.title: Notification hook for instant needs_attention detection
requirement.description: A new hook script (gmux-attention.sh) listens to Claude Code's Notification event and sends a needs_attention status via the gmux socket. This provides instant detection of permission dialogs without waiting for the 3s poll + heuristic cycle.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given Claude Code fires a Notification event (e.g., permission dialog), when gmux-attention.sh runs, then it sends {"event":"status","session":"...","pane":"...","status":"needs_attention"} to /tmp/gmux.sock.
Given the Notification hook fires, when gmux receives the socket event, then the session status immediately updates to needs_attention (no 3s poll delay).
Given the socket is unavailable, when gmux-attention.sh runs, then it exits 0 silently (fire-and-forget).

requirement.title: Hook detection at startup
requirement.description: On startup, gmux reads ~/.claude/settings.json and checks whether gmux hook entries are configured. If hooks are missing, a warning is shown in the header.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given ~/.claude/settings.json contains Stop and Notification hooks referencing gmux scripts, when gmux starts, then hooksConfigured is true and no warning is shown.
Given ~/.claude/settings.json does not exist, when gmux starts, then hooksConfigured is false and header shows "⚠ hooks" in yellow.
Given ~/.claude/settings.json exists but contains no gmux hook entries, when gmux starts, then hooksConfigured is false and header shows "⚠ hooks".
Given ~/.claude/settings.json contains malformed JSON, when gmux starts, then hooksConfigured is false (treated as missing). gmux does not crash.

requirement.title: gmux --setup-hooks CLI command
requirement.description: A CLI command that writes Stop and Notification hook entries into ~/.claude/settings.json at user scope. Resolves hook script paths to absolute. Idempotent — running twice does not duplicate entries. Preserves existing settings.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given ~/.claude/settings.json does not exist, when user runs gmux --setup-hooks, then the file is created with Stop and Notification hook entries pointing to absolute paths of gmux-status.sh and gmux-attention.sh.
Given ~/.claude/settings.json exists with other settings (e.g., permissions), when user runs gmux --setup-hooks, then gmux hook entries are added and existing settings are preserved.
Given gmux --setup-hooks has already been run, when user runs it again, then no duplicate entries are created (idempotent).
Given the write to settings.json fails (permission denied), when gmux --setup-hooks runs, then an error message is printed and the process exits with code 1. The original file is not corrupted.
Given gmux --setup-hooks succeeds, when the command completes, then a confirmation message is printed and the process exits with code 0 (no dashboard render).
